burgers_1d_li2021.title: 1-D viscous Burgers, Li et al. (2021) operator-learning benchmark (1200 trajectories, 1024 points)
burgers_1d_li2021.description: u_t + (u^2/2)_x = nu u_xx on the periodic interval [0, 1), nu = 0.1, t in [0, 1]. Initial conditions u0 ~ N(0, 625 (-Laplacian + 25 I)^-2), the input distribution stated in Li et al. (2021), section 5.1 (their released generator used alpha 2.5, tau 7, sigma 49 instead; this dataset follows the paper's text). The standard task maps u0 to u(., 1); the 11 snapshots t = 0, 0.1, ..., 1 are stored for time-dependent models. Grid x_j = j / 1024, j = 0..1023; u[:, 0] equals u0.
burgers_1d_li2021.source: python scripts/zoo/operator_data.py generate --out DIR (inputs drawn from fixed seeds in the parent process, so the data do not depend on the number of workers); solvers in pinneapple_simulation.numerical_solvers.operator_benchmarks, written from the equations; seed 20211
burgers_1d_li2021.verification: Solver (Fourier pseudo-spectral, 2/3 dealiasing, ETDRK4) checked in tests/test_operator_benchmarks.py against the Cole-Hopf exact solution (max error < 1e-8) and for exact mean conservation. Resolution and time-step study on 4 held-aside inputs against a reference with 4096 points and dt 2.5e-5, all 10 saved times: the dataset setting (1024 points, dt 1e-4) has max rel. L2 error 4.4e-12; halving dt gives 6.3e-13, doubling the points 4.4e-12 (time-step limited, spectrally converged in space). Mean conserved to 8e-17. Stored in float32 (rounding ~6e-8 relative), far below the 1e-3 to 1e-2 errors operator-learning methods reach on this task (scripts/zoo/operator_data.py convergence).
burgers_1d_li2021.citation: Li Z., Kovachki N., Azizzadenesheli K., Liu B., Bhattacharya K., Stuart A., Anandkumar A. (2021). Fourier Neural Operator for Parametric Partial Differential Equations. ICLR 2021, arXiv:2010.08895. Data generated with PINNeAPPle's reference solvers (pinneapple_simulation.numerical_solvers.operator_benchmarks); PINNeAPPle, Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23343062.

darcy_2d_li2021.title: 2-D Darcy flow, Li et al. (2021) operator-learning benchmark (1200 coefficient / pressure pairs, 128 x 128)
darcy_2d_li2021.description: -div(a grad u) = 1 on the unit square, u = 0 on the boundary. Coefficients a = 12 where g >= 0 and 3 where g < 0, g ~ N(0, (-Laplacian + 9 I)^-2) (Li et al. 2021, section 5.2). g is drawn as a periodic Gaussian random field on the 128 x 128 cell grid (Li et al. use a cosine expansion on 421 nodes), so a is piecewise constant on the cells of the stored grid. The task maps a to u. Cell centres ((i + 1/2) / 128, (j + 1/2) / 128); u is the cell average of the solution.
darcy_2d_li2021.source: python scripts/zoo/operator_data.py generate --out DIR (inputs drawn from fixed seeds in the parent process, so the data do not depend on the number of workers); solvers in pinneapple_simulation.numerical_solvers.operator_benchmarks, written from the equations; seed 20212
darcy_2d_li2021.verification: Solver (cell-centred two-point-flux finite volumes, harmonic face coefficients, sparse direct solve) checked in tests/test_operator_benchmarks.py on a manufactured variable-coefficient solution (second order, max error < 2e-3 at 64^2). Each sample is solved on the 512^2 grid (the piecewise-constant coefficient is represented exactly on every refinement) and averaged onto its 128^2 cells. Grid study on 4 held-aside inputs against 1024^2: max rel. L2 error 4.6e-3 (128^2), 1.6e-3 (256^2), 4.3e-4 (512^2, the dataset); observed order 1.36 / 1.21 (reduced from 2 by the coefficient jumps); Richardson estimate of the dataset's discretisation error ~8e-4 rel. L2, ten times below the ~1e-2 operator-learning methods reach on this task. u > 0 and below the a = 3 bound 1/24 in every sample.
darcy_2d_li2021.citation: Li Z., Kovachki N., Azizzadenesheli K., Liu B., Bhattacharya K., Stuart A., Anandkumar A. (2021). Fourier Neural Operator for Parametric Partial Differential Equations. ICLR 2021, arXiv:2010.08895. Data generated with PINNeAPPle's reference solvers (pinneapple_simulation.numerical_solvers.operator_benchmarks); PINNeAPPle, Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23343062.
darcy_2d_li2021.split_rule: rows 0-999 are train, 1000-1199 test; inputs are i.i.d. draws, so the contiguous split is a random split

navier_stokes_2d_li2021_nu1e-3.title: 2-D incompressible Navier-Stokes (vorticity), nu = 1e-3, Li et al. (2021) benchmark (1200 runs, 64 x 64, t 0-50)
navier_stokes_2d_li2021_nu1e-3.description: w_t + u . grad w = nu Laplacian(w) + f on the periodic unit square, u = (psi_y, -psi_x), -Laplacian(psi) = w, nu = 1e-3, f(x, y) = 0.1 (sin 2 pi (x + y) + cos 2 pi (x + y)), w0 ~ N(0, 7^(3/2) (-Laplacian + 49 I)^-2.5) (Li et al. 2021, section 5.3). Solved on 128 x 128 and stored on the 64 x 64 grid x_i = i / 64 at t = 0, 1, ..., 50 (51 snapshots; w[:, 0] is w0). The usual task maps the first 10 snapshots to the next 40, or w0 to w(., 50).
navier_stokes_2d_li2021_nu1e-3.source: python scripts/zoo/operator_data.py generate --out DIR (inputs drawn from fixed seeds in the parent process, so the data do not depend on the number of workers); solvers in pinneapple_simulation.numerical_solvers.operator_benchmarks, written from the equations; seed 20213
navier_stokes_2d_li2021_nu1e-3.verification: Solver (Fourier pseudo-spectral, 2/3 dealiasing, ETDRK4) checked in tests/test_operator_benchmarks.py: exact decay of a Taylor-Green vortex (1e-10) and a mean-free, finite forced flow. Resolution and time-step study on 4 held-aside inputs against a 256^2, dt 5e-3 reference at the stored 64^2 nodes and all 50 saved times: the dataset setting (128^2, dt 5e-2) has max rel. L2 error 4.0e-8 (6.6e-8 at t = 50); dt 2.5e-2 gives 2.5e-9 and dt 1e-2 6.0e-11 (fourth-order time convergence, the error is the time step's; the 128^2 grid is spectrally converged); solving directly on 64^2 would give 1.7e-4. Inputs are band-limited (Nyquist modes removed), so the 128^2 and 256^2 runs start from the same field. Every stored field is finite with spatial mean below 5e-8. Stored in float32 (~6e-8 relative), far below the 8e-3 or more operator-learning methods reach on this task.

airfoil_rans_cst_re4e6_fields.title: Airfoil RANS flow fields, CST shapes, Re 4e6 (436 OpenFOAM runs, 20064-cell O-grid)
airfoil_rans_cst_re4e6_fields.description: The cell fields of the 436-run airfoil campaign (dataset airfoil_rans_cst_re4e6): steady 2-D RANS, OpenFOAM v1912 simpleFoam, k-omega SST, y+ < 1, the shared 228 x 88 O-grid (20064 cells, far field 200 chords), 100 Latin-hypercube CST airfoils x 4 angles and NACA 0012/2412/4412/4415 x 9 angles. Per run: the 6 CST weights, the angle of attack, the final-iteration Cl, Cd, Cm, the run status (converged / steady-ish / unsteady), the cell centres x, y (the grid moves with the shape) and the kinematic pressure p, velocity Ux, Uy and eddy viscosity nut at every cell (free stream U = 1, chord 1). Cell order: wall-normal level j outer, around-the-airfoil index i inner (j * 228 + i).
airfoil_rans_cst_re4e6_fields.source: pinneapple_design.aero.dataset.plan(100, 4) (seed 7) run with dataset.run_job (apps/aero_optimizer/tools/generate_dataset.py), written by pinneapple_design.aero.field_dataset.write_field_dataset; same case set-up as the 436-run campaign of airfoil_rans_cst_re4e6
airfoil_rans_cst_re4e6_fields.verification: Regenerated with the campaign's case set-up; the 436 runs reproduce the coefficients of airfoil_rans_cst_re4e6 (median |dCl| 1.8e-7, median |dCd|/Cd 1.6e-6, same run status in all 436). The only differences above 1e-4 in Cl are 6 runs flagged unsteady, whose final-iteration values move within their recorded oscillation (largest |dCl| 0.037, NACA 0012 at 14 deg); filter on status for steady data. Solver verification of the campaign: grid study on NACA 2412 at alpha 4 deg (6840/20064/45144 cells: Cl 0.6614/0.6625/0.6624, Cd GCI 1.9 %, observed order 2.4), XFOIL 6.99 tripped (Cl -2.3 %, Cd +4.5 %), lift slope 0.110/deg as thin-airfoil theory, NASA TMR NACA 0012 SST (Cd 0.00812 vs 0.0081). Field checks: all values finite; far-field pressure 0 and total pressure 0.5 (U = 1); stagnation pressure within 2 % of 0.5 in 433 runs (max 0.527 in one converged run, 0.587 in an unsteady snapshot). Status: 330 converged, 74 steady-ish, 32 unsteady.
airfoil_rans_cst_re4e6_fields.citation: PINNeAPPle contributors (2026). Airfoil RANS campaign (OpenFOAM v1912 simpleFoam, k-omega SST, Re 4e6, 436 runs): flow fields and MeshGraphNet surrogate (Pfaff T., Fortunato M., Sanchez-Gonzalez A., Battaglia P., Learning Mesh-Based Simulation with Graph Networks, ICLR 2021). PINNeAPPle, Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23343062.

thermal_channel_cfd.title: Actuated heated-channel CFD, 2-D incompressible flow + heat (82 trajectories, 128 x 32, 101 snapshots)
thermal_channel_cfd.description: Non-dimensional channel [0, 10] x [0, 1], Re 100, Pr 0.71: parabolic inlet with time-varying mean velocity U(t) in [0.6, 1.4] and inlet temperature 0, no-slip walls, adiabatic except a heater on the bottom wall at x in [2, 4] with flux -dT/dy = Q(t) in [0, 2], zero-gradient outlet. After a 15-unit warm-up each trajectory records u, v, p, T on the 128 x 32 cell centres every 0.4 time units over 40 units (101 snapshots), with the actuators and the quantities of interest (bulk outlet temperature, maximum temperature, pressure drop, heat in / out, stored energy). Training actuation is random holds, steps and ramps; two test splits use families never seen in training (chirped sinusoids, steps between the range edges), for digital-twin and forecasting models. Cell centres and all solver settings are in meta.json; fields[:, k] is the state at t = 0.4 k.
thermal_channel_cfd.source: python scripts/zoo/thermal_channel_data.py generate --out DIR; recipe of PINNeAPPle-Benchmark experiment 05 (Apache-2.0) on pinneapple_simulation.numerical_solvers.thermal_channel_2d (staggered MAC grid, Chorin projection, dt 0.01), seeds per trajectory in pinneapple_simulation.numerical_solvers.thermal_channel_datasets.PLAN
thermal_channel_cfd.verification: Solver checks (python scripts/zoo/thermal_channel_data.py verify, pinneapple_simulation.numerical_solvers.thermal_channel_datasets.verify): plane Poiseuille flow, max error of the velocity profile 4.8e-3 / 1.3e-3 / 3.5e-4 on 64 x 16 / 128 x 32 (the dataset grid) / 256 x 64 (second order), dp/dx within 1.2 % of -12/Re, max divergence 1e-7; fully developed Nusselt number for one wall at uniform flux and one adiabatic, 5.392 / 5.388 vs 5.385 exact (Shah & London 1978), global energy imbalance 2.7e-8. Three-grid study of an actuated run (64 x 16, 128 x 32, 256 x 64, dt halved with h): GCI of the dataset grid 3.7 % for the bulk outlet temperature (oscillatory convergence, observed order 1.3), 1.1 % for the maximum temperature (order 2.3), 1.3 % for the pressure drop (order 1.3). In every trajectory the change of stored energy matches the trapezoidal integral of the recorded heat in - out to 0.3 % (median, smooth actuation) and at most 4 % (steps, limited by the 0.4 sampling of the actuators). All fields finite; float32 storage.
thermal_channel_cfd.citation: PINNeAPPle-Benchmark experiment 05 (actuated heated channel). Data generated with PINNeAPPle (pinneapple_simulation.numerical_solvers.thermal_channel_2d); PINNeAPPle, Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23343062.

cylinder_wake_lbm.title: Confined cylinder wake, lattice-Boltzmann, Re 20-100 (9 runs, 720 vorticity snapshots, 240 x 100)
cylinder_wake_lbm.description: 2-D flow past a cylinder (diameter D = 20 lattice cells) 3 D downstream of a uniform inlet in a channel 5 D high and 12 D long (blockage 0.2), no-slip walls, pressure outlet; D2Q9 BGK lattice-Boltzmann, inlet velocity 0.1 (Mach 0.17), no turbulence model. Each run covers 200 convective units (t U / D); the last 40 are stored (saturated wake), a vorticity snapshot (normalised by U/D, 0 inside the cylinder) every 0.5 units, labelled by Reynolds number, wake regime (steady or shedding), Strouhal number and wake amplitude. For regime classification, interpolation in Re and wake forecasting. The channel is far shorter than the entrance length, so the cylinder sees a nearly uniform inflow with thin wall boundary layers. Grid: x = i, y = j lattice cells, cylinder centre and solid cells in meta.json.
cylinder_wake_lbm.source: python scripts/zoo/cylinder_data.py generate --out DIR; pinneapple_simulation.numerical_solvers.cylinder_wake (the lab experiment cylinder_lbm runs the same function)
cylinder_wake_lbm.verification: Solver checks (python scripts/zoo/cylinder_data.py verify; pinneapple_simulation.numerical_solvers.cylinder_wake.verify): developed low-Re channel flow against plane Poiseuille, max profile error 7.6 % / 4.3 % on the 2x coarser / dataset grid (first order, full-way bounce-back walls), centreline over mean velocity 1.43 / 1.46 vs 1.5. Resolution study at Re 100 (D = 20, 30, 40 lattice cells, same physical time and sampling): Strouhal 0.2444 / 0.2458 / 0.2460, so the dataset grid (D = 20) is within 0.7 % of D = 40; vorticity rms 2 D behind the cylinder within 0.3 %; transverse-velocity rms within 6.7 % (0.9 % at D = 30). At Re 120, D = 20 gives a Strouhal number 4.4 % below D = 30 (relaxation time 0.55, near the stability limit), so the dataset stops at Re 100. Every shedding run is saturated: the probe rms changes by at most 5 % across the stored window; below the onset (Re <= 50, confinement delays it from the unconfined ~47) disturbances decay. Strouhal number from a Hann-windowed, peak-refined spectrum (raw FFT bins are 0.025 apart). All fields finite.
cylinder_wake_lbm.citation: Cylinder wake dataset generated with PINNeAPPle (pinneapple_simulation.numerical_solvers.cylinder_wake, D2Q9 lattice Boltzmann); PINNeAPPle, Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23343062.

blackhole_riaf_density_256.title: Accretion onto a Schwarzschild black hole: 2.5-D viscous hydro density frames (256 x 128)
blackhole_riaf_density_256.description: Radiatively inefficient accretion flow grown from an equilibrium torus (Paczynski-Wiita potential, Shakura-Sunyaev alpha viscosity, gamma 5/3, r = 4-400 GM/c^2, log-spaced 256 x 128 grid): the set-up of Duarte, Nemmen & Navarro (2022), regenerated with pinneapple_physics.blackhole. Density in the forecaster's window (r < 126.5 GM/c^2, theta in [pi/8, 7 pi/8]) every 20 GM/c^3 for t = 2000-10000 GM/c^3, whole trajectories per split. The training data of the black-hole weather forecaster (#399).
blackhole_riaf_density_256.source: examples/black_hole_weather/simulate.py --nr 256 --ntheta 128 --viscosity SS --perturbation-kind modes --t-end 10000 --every 10 (runs and seeds in pinneapple_physics.blackhole.dataset.SPLITS); scripts/zoo/build_blackhole.py
blackhole_riaf_density_256.verification: Solver: mass and angular momentum conserved to 1e-16 with the boundary fluxes counted, exact Bondi accretion steady within 0.5 %, inviscid torus in equilibrium (tests/test_blackhole_weather.py). Resolution study (examples/black_hole_weather/convergence.py; results/convergence.json): grids 90x45, 128x64, 181x90, 256x128 (ratio sqrt 2), seeds 0-2 on every grid with the same seeded perturbation, time averages over t = 2000-10000 GM/c^3 with 95 % intervals (batch means and seeds). Converged within the statistical band (the two finest grids agree within their intervals): mean accretion rate 2.18 +- 0.58 (181) vs 1.97 +- 0.63 (256), window mass 2.65e4 vs 2.58e4, inner density slope -0.41 vs -0.38, persistence error at 100 GM/c^3 0.0034 +- 0.0011 vs 0.0047 +- 0.0011. Not converged: from 181 to 256 the time-mean profiles change more than between the coarser grids (density 6.3 % vs 0.8-1.6 %, specific angular momentum 4.2 % vs 0.5 %, angular-momentum flux 11 % vs 1.5-2.5 %; l / l_Kepler at r = 10 rises 3.8 % beyond its interval), so the observed order is negative and no GCI applies; the number of cells where the speed / temperature ceilings act grows with resolution and is the likely cause. The 256 x 128 grid is the finest the study could afford (a 362 x 181 run did not finish); the 181 -> 256 changes are the uncertainty band of these data. The published PLUTO runs and the paper's values could not be retrieved for a direct comparison.
blackhole_riaf_density_256.citation: Duarte R., Nemmen R., Navarro J. P. (2022) MNRAS 512, 5848 (set-up and forecaster); Almeida I., Nemmen R. (2020) MNRAS 492, 2553 (simulations); data generated with PINNeAPPle, Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23343062.
blackhole_riaf_density_256.split_rule: by trajectory (seed), never by time inside a trajectory: train seeds 0-3, val 4, test 5

convergence.description: resolution study: one row per grid and seed (90x45 to 256x128, seeds 0-2)

ood_alpha0.3.description: alpha 0.3, seed 0: other physics, never used in training

train.description: seeds 0-3, alpha 0.1: 4 whole trajectories, 401 frames each

ell_over_kepler_r10.description: time-mean specific angular momentum / Keplerian (Paczynski-Wiita), r = 10

mdot_detrended_rms.description: rms of mdot / (500 GM/c^3 running mean) - 1

mdot_psd_slope.description: log-log slope of the accretion-rate power spectrum, 1/2000 to 1/50 per GM/c^3

mdot_rms_over_mean.description: rms / mean of the accretion rate (includes the secular drain of the torus)

persistence_mae_20M.description: MAE of persistence at 20 GM/c^3 (normalised log density, log10 rho in [-6, 0])

rho_slope_r10_60.description: d ln rho / d ln r of the time-mean shell density, r = 10-60 GM/c^2

r.description: radius of the cell centres (volume weighted)

theta.description: polar angle of the cell centres

log10_rho_q.description: uint16 (frames, 192 r, 96 theta): log10 rho = -8 + q * 9 / 65535 in the window (pinneapple_physics.blackhole.dataset.decode)

mdot.description: accretion rate through r_in = 4 GM/c^2 (density maximum of the initial torus = 1)

run.description: trajectory: the seed of the initial torus perturbation
